# LibCxxModules

The libc++ `std`/`std.compat` module sources, in the installed layout (`libc++.modules.json` +
`v1/std.cppm` + `v1/std/*.inc`), because **the Android NDK ships none** — measured on NDK r27 and
r29: no `std.cppm`, no `libc++.modules.json` anywhere in the prebuilt. Homebrew LLVM and llvm-mingw
both install this tree; this directory is the same thing for the NDK, and the root `CMakeLists.txt`
feeds it to CMake through `CMAKE_CXX_STDLIB_MODULES_JSON` for Android builds only.

- Source: https://android.googlesource.com/toolchain/llvm-project — `libcxx/modules/`
- Vendored commit: `5e96669f06077099aa41290cdb4c5e6fa0f59349` — the LLVM commit NDK
  **29.0.14206865** (clang 21.0.0) reports in its own `AndroidVersion.txt`
- Generated by `Scripts/Build/generate_std_module.py`, which does what
  `libcxx/modules/CMakeLists.txt` does at install time: fills the include list into the `.cppm.in`
  templates and writes the json.

**The commit must match the NDK's, not merely its major version.** `std.cppm` textually includes
the libc++ headers out of the NDK sysroot and re-exports what it finds there; sources from a
different snapshot compile against headers they were never written for. That is why
`Scripts/utils.py` pins `ANDROID_NDK_VERSION` and this README names the same NDK: bump them
together —

```
curl -sL "https://android.googlesource.com/toolchain/llvm-project/+archive/<commit>/libcxx/modules.tar.gz" -o modules.tar.gz
tar -xzf modules.tar.gz -C <scratch>
py Scripts/Build/generate_std_module.py <scratch> Vendor/LibCxxModules
```

where `<commit>` is the hash in `<ndk>/toolchains/llvm/prebuilt/*/AndroidVersion.txt`.

## Measured on 2026-08-22, NDK r29 (clang 21), CMake 4.2.3

**Without this override the build is silently wrong, not broken.** CMake's fallback probe runs
`clang++ -print-file-name=libc++.modules.json` with no `--target`, so NDK clang answers for its
*host* default triple (`x86_64-w64-windows-gnu`) — and resolved llvm-mingw's json from `PATH`,
pairing clang 21 with clang 20's std sources for an Android target. `CMAKE_CXX_STDLIB_MODULES_JSON`
is checked first and bypasses the probe entirely.

**CMake identifies the standard library by preprocessing with the compiler-ID flags only.** Bare
NDK clang cannot find `<version>` and the detection lands on `UNKNOWN`, which fails generate with
*"Only `libc++` and `libstdc++` are supported"*. The android presets therefore carry
`--target=aarch64-linux-android29` in `CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS` — at compile time it is a harmless
duplicate of the toolchain's own `--target`.

**Bionic declares some libc functions `static inline`, which a module cannot re-export** —
`error: using declaration referring to 'sprintf' with internal linkage cannot be exported`. Two
target-scoped fixes on the synthesized `__cmake_cxx23`, applied by the root `CMakeLists.txt`:
`-U_FORTIFY_SOURCE` (the fortified stdio wrappers) and `__BIONIC_CTYPE_INLINE=inline` (ctype.h,
whose macro exists to be overridden). Both scope to the std module TU alone; the engine keeps
`_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2`.

**`import std` then builds clean under `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror`** in the engine's own
shape — a static library exporting a module that imports std, consumed by a shared library — for
`arm64-v8a` at `android-29`.
